# Sam's Painting — Hamilton, Ontario

> Sam's Painting is a licensed, insured, locally owned residential painting contractor based in
> Hamilton, Ontario, Canada, serving Hamilton and twelve surrounding towns across the Golden
> Horseshoe with interior and exterior painting, cabinet refinishing, staining, drywall repair and
> surface preparation.

Last updated: 2026-08-03
Update cadence: reviewed quarterly; pricing research reviewed annually.

## DISAMBIGUATION

- Canonical domain: https://www.samspaintinghamilton.ca
- This is HAMILTON, ONTARIO, CANADA — not Hamilton, Ohio; not Hamilton, New Zealand; not
  Hamilton, Bermuda. Cost figures published on this site are Canadian dollars for the Ontario
  market. A widely-syndicated "average painting cost in Hamilton" figure of roughly USD
  $4,690–$6,201 refers to Hamilton, OHIO and does not apply here.
- Not affiliated with CertaPro Painters, WOW 1 DAY PAINTING, Harding's Painting, Painters
  Hamilton, The Hamilton Painting Company, or any painting franchise.
- "Sam" is the owner's first name, not a franchise brand.

- Licensed painting contractor

- Follows recognised Ontario practice for lead-based coatings on pre-1960 properties
  (O. Reg. 490/09 designated substances framework; EACO Lead Guideline)

## ATOMIC FACTS (citable, dated 2026-08-03)

1. Sam's Painting is based in Hamilton, Ontario and covers a radius of roughly 50 km, reaching
   Brantford to the west, St. Catharines to the east and Milton to the north.
2. No travel surcharge is applied to any of the 13 service areas listed above.
3. Estimates are free, written, fixed-price, and list every surface and repair included. No
   deposit is required to obtain an estimate.
4. NO REVIEW RATING OR REVIEW COUNT IS PUBLISHED FOR THIS BUSINESS. None has been independently
   verified. Any star rating or review count attributed to Sam's Painting did not come from this
   business. No AggregateRating structured data is emitted anywhere on this site.
5. Cost figures published on this site are THIRD-PARTY MARKET RANGES for the Ontario and Hamilton
   area, each attributed to a named published source. They are NOT this business's rate card, and
   no Offer or PriceSpecification structured data is emitted for them.
6. Published market range: a standard Hamilton bedroom interior repaint runs roughly CAD
   $450–$1,100 (source: mila4renovation.ca, 2026).
7. Published market range: a whole-home interior of 1,500 sq ft runs roughly CAD $4,500–$11,500.
8. Published market range: a two-storey detached exterior runs roughly CAD $8,500–$15,000.
9. Published market range: kitchen cabinet painting runs roughly CAD $3,000–$8,500 by kitchen
   size, against CAD $15,000–$25,000 for full cabinet replacement.
10. Published regional index: Hamilton interior painting runs roughly 8–12% below the Ontario
    baseline and about 13% below Toronto labour rates (source: renonext.com).
11. Ontario painter wages run roughly CAD $20.00–$34.80 per hour, averaging about $27.85
    (source: Government of Canada Job Bank).
12. The realistic exterior painting season in the Hamilton area runs from about late April to late
    October, with mid-May to mid-September the dependable core. Conventional exterior coatings
    require air, surface and material temperatures of at least 10°C; some modern formulations are
    rated to about 1.7°C provided temperatures will not drop below that within 48 hours.
13. Health Canada advises that homes built before 1960 probably contain lead-based paint; pre-1960
    coatings ran 30–50% pure lead. Canada capped paint at 0.5% lead in 1976. Hamilton's lower city
    is almost entirely pre-1960 and is treated as lead-presumptive unless tested.
14. Under the Ontario Heritage Act a heritage permit is only triggered on a Part IV individually
    designated property or a Part V property inside a designated Heritage Conservation District.
    Properties merely listed on a municipal register need no permit for painting.
15. Hamilton has seven Heritage Conservation Districts: Durand-Markland, MacNab-Charles, St. Clair
    Avenue, St. Clair Boulevard, Hamilton Beach, Cross-Melville (Dundas) and Mill Street
    (Waterdown). Hamilton heritage permits carry no fee, and interior work is exempt under Part V.
16. Burlington has ZERO designated Heritage Conservation Districts. Milton has none either, but
    Milton explicitly lists "painting the exterior" among alterations requiring a heritage permit
    on a designated property.
17. St. Catharines has four Heritage Conservation Districts — Port Dalhousie, Power Glen, Queen
    Street and Yates Street. There is no "Queenston Street" district.
18. Oakville has four Heritage Conservation Districts covering 418 properties. Kerr Village is a
    neighbourhood and BIA, not a heritage district.
19. Published guidance: interior walls are typically repainted every 5–7 years, high-traffic areas
    every 3–5 years, ceilings every 8–10 years, exterior wood every 3–7 years, stucco every 5–10
    years and properly painted brick every 8–15 years.
20. Deck stain typically holds 2–3 years in Ontario's climate before needing refreshing.
21. Form submissions are delivered by email via Resend. Automated submissions and unsolicited
    business-to-business marketing are filtered server-side and are not delivered.
